subject: Reserved commit term & staggered capacity start proposal
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@novagrid.ai
Date: 2027-09-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — dedicated reserved commit options and staggered start

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — NovaGrid is excited about Redwood's latency profile. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask so we can align internal approvals.

High level: we expect to start with a Dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads (mix of chat and embeddings). Rough sizing estimate is ~8–12 A10G-equivalent GPUs initially, growing to ~24 within the first 9 months.

Questions we need answered to move toward PO/Legal:
- Pricing bands for reserved commits for 12 / 24 / 36 month terms (we prefer to see unit pricing at committed GPU-months).
- Options for a staggered / soft start (i.e., ability to ramp to full capacity over a 60–120 day window) and how that affects pricing and credits.
- Throughput/latency guarantees and what remedies are available if commitments aren’t met.
- Any minimum notice or hard start date requirements for a Dedicated pool.

Can you share a concise proposal and SLA draft? We’d like to circulate internally this week. We’ve looped procurement on cc.

Best,
Elena Torres
Head of Platform — NovaGrid
elena@novagrid.ai

Attachment: RFP_Requests_NovaGrid_0909.pdf (referenced)

From: mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-12T11:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — dedicated reserved commit options and staggered start

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the headroom signal. Quick summary below; I attached a short pricing matrix and a first-pass SLA for your review.

TL;DR (options):
- 12-month reserved commit: unit price = $6,200 / GPU-month (baseline). Short ramp window (30 days) included.
- 24-month reserved commit: unit price = $5,450 / GPU-month (~12% discount vs 12mo). Staggered start up to 90 days without penalty if we agree a ramp plan.
- 36-month reserved commit: unit price = $4,980 / GPU-month (~20% discount vs 12mo). Includes a 120-day soft-start allowance and 2x burst credits during first 60 days for traffic spikes.

Ramp constructs we offer:
- Soft-start (recommended for your growth pattern): phased capacity activation with predefined milestones (e.g., 30% active month 1, 60% month 2, 100% by month 3) and pro-rated billing for months where capacity is not fully active.
- Start-gate: an agreed date where committed capacity transitions from staging to production; up to two start-gate pushes allowed with 30 days notice.

Throughput & SLA highlights:
- We can commit to a throughput floor per GPU-profile (e.g., A10G): expected median throughput and 95th percentile latency for the 512-token nominal prompt. SLA in the attached doc enumerates remedies (service credits tied to p95/p99 latency bands and availability for your reserved pool).

Next steps I propose:
1) Review attached pricing matrix and SLA draft (RGX_NovaGrid_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.pdf, RGX_SLA_Draft_NovaGrid.docx).
2) Tell us your preferred term (12/24/36) and an initial activation timetable (preferred start-gate window).
3) If acceptable, we’ll produce a redline-ready commercial term sheet and iterate on ramp milestones.

Attaching: RGX_NovaGrid_Dedicated_Pricing_v1.pdf, RGX_SLA_Draft_NovaGrid.docx

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0128

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>, mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-09-13T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — dedicated reserved commit options and staggered start

Elena — quick follow with a commercial counter-proposal and some flexibility notes from our side.

Commercial counter (high level):
- 24-month target we recommend given your growth profile: 16 GPU-months committed in first quarter, ramp to 48 GPU-months by month 9.
- If you sign 24 months we can offer a tiered discount ladder: 10% off list for the first 12 months, 14% off base rate for months 13–24 contingent on hitting the ramp milestones.
- For 36 months we’ll entertain an initial one-time credit (amount applied to the first invoice) in lieu of deeper monthly discount; useful if you want to preserve cashflow.

On staggered starts and credits:
- We can formalize a soft-start with three ramp checkpoints (30d/90d/180d). Billing is pro-rated by active GPU-hours. If we miss agreed activation milestones (Redwood side) we provide a ramp-failure credit to offset the first full invoice month up to 20% of that month’s charge.

Throughput guarantees (practical):
- We do not guarantee absolute tokens/sec across mixed workloads without baseline telemetry. Instead, we guarantee a p95 latency band per model class for your committed pool, and provide a remediation credit schedule if the p95 band is missed across a rolling 7-day window.
- We also include a performance playbook in onboarding: model footprints, quantization profiles, and recommended kernel sets so we can hit your throughput targets faster.

Operational asks from NovaGrid (what we need to finalize pricing):
1) Concrete target start-gate (month/day).
2) Expected model mix (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) and average token length.
3) Any compliance add-ons that would change infra (private VPC, longer logs retention).

I’ll circulate a marked term sheet after we get those items. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call with procurement to accelerate.

—Marissa
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: nova-prod-onboarding-mop.xlsx (onboarding milestones workbook)

From: Elena Torres <elena@novagrid.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — dedicated reserved commit options and staggered start

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from procurement and infra: 

1) Throughput/latency: we will provide a short benchmark set (typical prompts + 1k example queries) — can you confirm whether the p95 remedy is an invoice credit only or if there is an operational escalation path (e.g., increased CPU/GPU allocation while we troubleshoot)?
2) Ramp-failure credit: your 20% cap sounds reasonable; can that be applied as a credit against future invoices (not retroactive cash refund)?
3) Start-gate: our preferred target is Oct 15, 2027 but we can shift by +/- 21 days. Can you confirm required notice and any constraints for hardware allocation?

We’ll collect the model mix and the benchmark set and share by EOD Friday.

Regards,
Elena

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — dedicated reserved commit options and staggered start

Elena — quick alignment from the product/ops side to close the loop on the start-gate and escalation mechanics.

Notice & allocation constraints:
- Required procurement notice to guarantee a Dedicated pool: 21 calendar days to provision an initial pool up to 16 A10G-equivalent GPUs in our standard quota. For larger initial pools (>= 24 GPUs) we request 45 days lead time to secure capacity across availability zones.

Operational escalation and performance credits:
- Remediation path: if your benchmark shows missed p95 bands, our first step is an operational escalation (priority triage, temporary scaling to absorb burst traffic, and model-specific tuning). If the issue persists after a 7-day triage window, credits apply as per the SLA (credits are applied to future invoices).
- Ramp-failure credits are applied as a future-invoice credit only (no cash refunds). The 20% cap Marissa mentioned is per affected invoice month.

Start-gate response:
- Oct 15, 2027 is feasible for an initial pool up to 16 GPUs with our 21-day notice requirement; for your stated desire to scale to ~24 GPUs by month 9 we recommend locking a 24-month term to preserve pricing and capacity priority.

Operational checklist (what we’ll need next):
1) Benchmark bundle (once you share, our infra team will run in our staging pool to baseline).
2) Signed term sheet indicating term length and rough ramp milestones.
3) PO or commitment letter so procurement has visibility while Legal prepares contract redlines.

If that all looks good, I’ll create a short execution plan and route to our legal ops for a draft SOW/term sheet.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product Partnerships — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
